references.text: David expresses trust that only God can forgive sins, which reflects the question of who can forgive sins in Mark 2:7.
God proclaims his ability to blot out transgressions, underscoring his unique authority to forgive sins, as challenged in Mark 2:7.
The Lord's promise to forgive sins and remember them no more, reflecting the question of divine authority to forgive sins in Mark 2:7.
Jesus forgives a paralyzed man's sins and heals him, directly demonstrating Jesus' authority to forgive sins, which is the theme of Mark 2:7.
Jesus forgives sins and heals a paralyzed man, confirming his authority to forgive sins, parallel to Mark 2:7.
Peter speaks of Jesus as Lord and Christ who forgives sins, reflecting the discussion about who can forgive sins in Mark 2:7.
